rationale: Temperature 0.9 sits in the high-creativity band (0.9-1.5) but stays below 1.0-1.2 where GPT-2 starts to lose coherence, so intros gain personality without turning to gibberish. Top-p 0.95 with top-k disabled lets the candidate vocabulary widen when the model is uncertain (opening hooks, metaphors) and shrink when the next word is obvious, which is why nucleus sampling reads more natural than a fixed top-k cut-off. Trade-off: more variety and engagement means less predictability and a higher chance of off-topic or unsupported claims, so a human edit pass is still needed. This serves the marketing complaint that intros sound robotic and boring.

Temperature 0.3 lies in the low band (0.2-0.5) that favours the highest-probability tokens, giving clear, factual, professional wording and reducing invented specifications; going below about 0.1 would cause repetition. Top-p 0.9 trims the unlikely long tail of tokens (where fabricated terms live) while leaving enough choice to avoid stilted phrasing; top-k is disabled because nucleus sampling adapts to context. Trade-off: text is less colourful and more repetitive, which is acceptable for documentation. For fully reproducible output, beam search (num_beams 3-5) is a good alternative. This serves clients who reported outputs that were too creative.

Temperature 0.6 is in the middle band (0.6-0.8): warm and natural enough to avoid the cold, overly formal tone, yet controlled enough to stay on topic. Top-p 0.85 is tighter than the creative setting, so casual or off-topic words in the tail are excluded while the reply keeps some natural phrasing; top-k is disabled so the vocabulary adapts to each question (password reset vs billing). Trade-off: slightly less personality than creative copy and slightly less consistency than a technical setting. Values near 1.2 risked becoming too casual or drifting off topic. This serves the support complaint of being either too formal or too casual.
